children: The centre is expected to create around 800 high-value technology jobs, with a reported median annual salary of Rs 35 lakh

Starbucks has signed a memorandum of understanding with the Tamil Nadu government to establish its first Global Capability Centre (GCC) in India in Chennai, expanding its global technology operations beyond the United States.

The centre is expected to create around 800 jobs in its initial phase. It will support Starbucks’ global operations, with planned focus areas including technology, analytics, finance, software development and research and development.

The proposed hub is expected to be located at Ramanujan IT Park in Taramani, according to media reports. The roles are expected to be high-value technology positions, with reports citing a median annual salary of around Rs 35 lakh. Recruitment is expected to begin in the first quarter of 2027. These are projected figures for the proposed centre, not jobs already created.

The Chennai facility will complement Starbucks’ existing technology hubs in Seattle and Nashville, forming part of its wider global capability network. The company has cited Chennai’s technology talent pool, engineering ecosystem, infrastructure and academic institutions among the factors behind its choice of location.

The GCC will operate separately from Tata Starbucks, the company’s Indian retail joint venture with Tata Consumer Products, which runs Starbucks cafés in India. The new centre is intended to serve Starbucks’ global operations rather than only its domestic retail business.

The announcement adds to Chennai’s growing role as a destination for multinational capability centres, with companies using India-based hubs for technology, analytics, finance and other global functions. The proposed Starbucks centre is expected to add to demand for skilled technology professionals in the city.
